questions.question: What is a "school of thought" according to Oyeshile & Ugwuanyi (2006)?

options.A: A temporary trend in philosophical discussions
options.B: Views held by a group for a long time that survive the test of time

questions.question: Who is the main proponent of Idealism?
Plato's Allegory of the Cave primarily illustrates:

options.B: The distinction between the world of senses and the world of ideas
options.C: The role of skepticism in acquiring knowledge
options.D: The scientific method for discovering truth

questions.question: Which school of thought emphasizes that "matter is independent of the mind"?
Aristotle's theory posits that objects are composed of:
Thomas Aquinas's Summa Theologica is best described as:

options.B: A synthesis of Aristotle's philosophy and Christian theology

questions.question: Skepticism, as described in the text, argues that:

options.B: Doubt is unnecessary when evidence is provided
options.C: Human knowledge is limited and uncertain
options.D: Faith alone can reveal ultimate truths

questions.question: Who introduced the inductive methodology (scientific method) into modern realism?
John Locke's concept of tabula rasa refers to:

options.A: The mind as a blank slate shaped by experience
options.B: The innate ideas present at birth
options.D: The divine origin of human reasoning

questions.question: According to Plato, a priori truths include:

options.B: To every proposition, there is an equal opposition
options.C: The physical world is the only reality

questions.question: Which philosopher argued that the universe has a design and a First Cause (Unmoved Mover)?
Realism, as opposed to Idealism, asserts that:

options.B: Objects exist independently of human perception
options.C: Knowledge is derived purely from faith
options.D: Abstract ideas are more real than physical objects
